title: docs/guide-anchors.md: for Linus and the other anchors
description: Flag day: register and merge first with anchors.json, approve the first maintainers, switch gpg.ssh.allowedSignersFile to the --min-tier maintainer export, release tooling to --min-tier anchor, sign the first SSH release tag. Day to day: approving and demoting maintainers, revoking a compromised key, reading check warnings in registry merges, sync. Rotation, endorsing, lost key.
acceptance_criteria: All commands run successfully in a throwaway registry (doc test); links to vouching.md.
notes:
Patch signing (patatt/b4) sections are added later by vouch-mzkw.5 once the patatt fork exists; do not write patatt instructions in this bead (they could not be doc-tested yet).
QUESTION (doc test, 2026-10-22): under DST (host TZ America/Vancouver, OpenSSH 9.6p1, git 2.55) git passes verify-time as local time without a zone and ssh-keygen reads it an hour late, so a signature made within the hour before its key's valid-before (retirement, demotion, removal) fails git verify-tag. Not a git-vouch bug; test pins TZ=UTC. Owner's call whether docs should warn or git-vouch should do anything.
QUESTION: a record signed by a key that is later revoked AND retired, dated in the same second as the retirement, fails check as an error ('dated outside the validity') instead of being void. Real-world negligible (one-second window); seen only when the doc test compressed steps. Test spaces steps one second apart.
QUESTION (owner's call, design semantics): check voids an endorsement whose subjectKey is later revoked (git-vouch endorsement loop, 'void: <did> of <h> is revoked'), so a lost-key recovery un-endorses the person and drops their email principal until re-endorsed. DESIGN.md's Endorsement bullets say endorsements carry over to later keys, also across an unsigned warned change, and list only the endorser's key being revoked as voiding. Should revoking the subject's key void endorsements naming it? Guide currently describes this as present tool behaviour pending that decision, and re-endorses (correct either way).
